category_title: At-risk students in Applied courses with learned helplessness and inconsistent engagement
student_description: This student struggles with deeply ingrained learned helplessness, compartmentalized thinking, and a severe fear of being wrong in front of peers. They attribute academic struggles to internal flaws (e.g., being 'stupid') and cannot independently transfer concepts across subjects. To succeed, they uniquely require private verification of accuracy before public sharing, integration of personal experiences to build competence, and explicit, tutor-driven connections between subjects.

criteria.rationale: Because the student severely compartmentalizes learning ('I learn Math here and I do Math here'), the tutor must take long-term responsibility for weaving subjects together.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes explicitly mapping and referencing concepts across different subjects or domains (e.g., parallel lesson planning) to continuously demonstrate how they connect.

criteria.rationale: The student's learned helplessness means they will consistently fail and shut down if expected to independently transfer knowledge over time.
criteria.check: The long-term plan explicitly avoids relying on the student to independently transfer knowledge, instead detailing how the tutor will consistently model and explicitly state connections.
